newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Community rules allow independent resales of new cars - Court.
newsitem.headline: Community rules allow independent resales of new cars - Court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Community rules governing car distribution do not prevent independent traders from reselling new cars.

French car dealers challenged as anti-competitive the activity of a parallel importer, Aqueducs Automobiles, which sells and advertises for sale cars registered for less than three months or having less than 3000 kilometres on the clock.
French law expanded the definition of new cars to those with less than 6000 kilometres on the clock or under six months old, with a view to impeding parallel sales, the court said.
The dealers argued that Community law prevents an independent dealer from keeping an inventory of new vehicles for sale without an identified final purchaser.

The court followed its earlier ruling in Nissan v France (C-309/94) and agreed with Aquedec that Community rules governing car distribution only pertain to contractual relations between manufacturers and distributors, not independent resellers.

The court said that since Commission regulation No 123/85 does not govern parallel imports and their resale by independent dealers, there is no point in defining what is a new or second-hand car under this regulation.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)

"Competition - Vehicle distribution - Parallel imports - Regulation (EEC) No 123/85 - Applicability as against third parties - Independent reseller - Definition of "new vehicle" and "second-hand vehicle"
Reference from the Tribunal de Commerce, Lyon, France for a preliminary ruling between
Fontaine SA, Garage Laval SA, Faby SA, Renault Lyon Ouest FLB Automobiles SA, Diffusion Vallis Auto SA, Horizon Sud SA

on the interpretation of Commission regulation (EEC) No 124/85 of 12 December 1984 on the application of article 85(3) of the EEC Treaty to certain categories of motor vehicle distribution and servicing agreements (OJ 1985 L 15, p. 16)

Commission regulation (EEC) No 124/85 of 12 December 1984 on the application of article 85(3) of the EEC Treaty to certain categories of motor vehicle distribution and servicing agreements is to be interpreted as not preventing a trader who is neither an approved reseller in the distribution network of a manufacturer of a particular make of motor vehicle nor an authorized intermediary within the meaning of article 3(11) of that regulation from undertaking parallel imports and opeating as an independent reseller of new vehicles of that make.
